passage:
Monday. After failing the lab test, Siddharth stuck a note on his mirror: "I am AMAZING!" It felt like lying, and he tore it off.
Thursday. Awake at 3 am, he remembered what he had told Pradeep last month: "You're worn out, not worthless. Eat something and sleep." He said the same words to himself, quietly. In the morning he ate dal and rice, took a short walk and texted Pradeep, "Bad week. Free for chai?"
Two weeks later. Some mornings were still heavy. Siddharth noticed that being kind to himself helped but did not lift everything, so he booked a slot with the campus counsellor. "Small kindness first, real help too," he wrote on his hand, and went.

qa.q: What did Siddharth stick on his mirror on Monday?
qa.a: He stuck a note saying "I am AMAZING!" on his mirror.

qa.q: Why did Siddharth tear off the note?
qa.a: Siddharth felt low after failing the lab test, and the forced cheer of the note felt like lying, so it did not ring true.

qa.q: Why was booking the campus counsellor a sensible step?
qa.a: Kindness to himself helped but did not lift everything, so professional help added what self-talk could not.

qa.q: How might Pradeep feel receiving the chai text?
qa.a: Glad to be trusted with "Bad week", and perhaps happy to return the care Siddharth had once shown Pradeep.

grounding: The protagonist replaces forced positivity with speaking to himself as to a friend, adds small kind acts and turns to a counsellor.
